The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) announced today (25 November) the official launch of CMU Digital Asset Platform (CMU DAP). Developed and operated by CMU OmniClear Limited (CMU OmniClear) on behalf of the HKMA, this distributed ledger technology (DLT)-based platform of the Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU) represents a major milestone in advancing the digital landscape of Hong Kong’s financial market.

CMU DAP not only facilitates a paperless process spanning debt securities primary issuance, clearing and settlement of secondary transactions, coupon payment and redemption at maturity, but also supports the tokenisation of traditional debt securities to bridge digital finance and traditional finance. Adopting an atomic Delivery versus Payment (DvP) on-chain settlement model, CMU DAP has direct interfaces with the Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) systems and central bank digital currencies (CBDC), and supports 24-hour settlement in multi-currencies using cash tokens, significantly enhancing market liquidity, operational efficiency and flexibility.

Following the USM launch, Hong Kong Securities Clearing Company Limited (“HKSCC”) would like to remind HKSCC Participants (“Participants”) of the following requirements when delivering physical certificates and supporting documents to the Depository Counter. These requirements are intended to enhance Participants’ service experience, shorten the processing time and minimize the risk of deposit rejection or delay.

Participants should use the updated STF for applicable deposit and dematerialization requests submitted to the Depository Counter. Please refer to HKSCC circular ( PT/DPS/CCASS/012/2026 ) for details and the prescribed form attached.

Physical deposit form is no longer accepted. Participants should input and authorize each deposit/demat order through the “Login Deposit/Demat Order” function in CCASS before delivering the corresponding physical certificates and supporting documents to the Depository Counter. Participants should ensure that the information entered in CCASS is complete, accurate and consistent with the certificates and supporting documents.

For deposits of non-participating securities, Participants should select the appropriate option in the “Change of Beneficial Ownership” field in CCASS. To mitigate the added risk associated with large cleared portfolios, OTC Clear imposes a margin add-on on portfolios that present material liquidation risk in the potential event of default. Based on the poll results, OTC Clear calibrates the required levels of margin add-on with respect to the different level of risks as reflected by the Initial Margin requirements. OTC Clear will apply the relevant Liquidity Risk Multiplier to calculate a margin add-on for the entire cleared portfolio (Portfolio Level Add-on) and a margin add-on with reference to the product group within the cleared portfolio (Component Level Add-on). OTC Clearing Hong Kong Limited (“ OTC Clear ”) is pleased to announce the rollout of client buffer service and the non-cash collateral withdrawal enhancement, as detailed below:

Both the client buffer service and the non-cash collateral withdrawal enhancement will take effect on 23 November 2026.

items.source_excerpt:
The Government welcomed the passage of the Banking Legislation (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill 2026 by the Legislative Council today (18 November). This will enable Hong Kong’s banking legislation to keep abreast of the times, better cater for the future development needs of the banking industry, and further align with the regulatory regimes of other major international financial centres.

The Banking Legislation (Miscellaneous Amendments) Ordinance 2026 (Amendment Ordinance) has fully taken into account the operation and regulatory environment of the banking industry in Hong Kong, and has made reference to relevant international standards and practices. The Amendment Ordinance amends the Banking Ordinance in the following areas: (i) regulation of bank holding companies; (ii) engagement of skilled persons for supervisory purposes; (iii) modernisation of enforcement provisions; (iv) simplification of the current three-tier banking system into a two-tier system; and (v) technical amendments to reduce compliance burden and enhance regulatory clarity and effectiveness. The Amendment Ordinance also makes amendments to The Hong Kong Association of Banks Ordinance and the Financial Institutions (Resolution) Ordinance for enhancing operational efficiency and flexibility.

The Amendment Ordinance will come into operation in phases starting from 1 January 2027.

items.source_excerpt:
The report, building on the HKIMR’s prior study published in 2025,1 provides an updated overview of the Generative A.I. (GenA.I.) landscape and explores agentic A.I. developments in Hong Kong’s financial services industry. It places particular emphasis on the application of A.I. in regulatory compliance. The report draws on comprehensive insights from a survey and in-depth interviews commissioned by the HKIMR, conducted between January and July 2026 with financial institutions and technology and Regtech service providers.

The report underscores sustained momentum for GenA.I. adoption in Hong Kong’s financial services industry, with current or planned adoption reaching 90%, up from 75% in 2025.2 Meanwhile, agentic A.I. adoption is growing, with 13% of financial institutions having already implemented and 56% planning to implement the technology. Looking ahead, over half of the surveyed financial institutions would prioritise GenA.I. and explore agentic A.I., while some others indicated a balanced approach between the two.

Within the regulatory compliance space, 86% of the surveyed financial institutions have adopted or plan to adopt GenA.I. solutions, and over 70% expressed interest in exploring the use of agentic A.I. over the next three to five years.

There are still challenges hindering the further adoption of GenA.I. and agentic A.I., such as concerns regarding explainability and security.

The report is available on the AoF/HKIMR website.

Hong Kong Academy of Finance

Following the successful completion of two Market Rehearsals (Ref. No. HDS/26/0904 & HDS/26/1005 ), Hosting Services is pleased to announce the commencement of the Network Equipment Replacement for HSN Services.

The replacement will be carried out over two consecutive weekends, with a mandatory Post Release Test (“PRT”) to be conducted following each replacement activity on 5 December 2026 and 12 December 2026 (Saturdays) . All HSN Subscribers are required to participate in both PRTs.

The HSN Primary Link will be migrated to the new hardware during PRT1, while the Secondary Link will remain connected to the existing hardware. The Secondary Link will subsequently be migrated to the new hardware during PRT2. The migrated link(s) will remain on the new hardware after each PRT, with no fallback to the existing hardware.

All HSN Subscribers are required to test their HSN connectivity to the relevant HKEX Market Systems during PRT, as applicable to their daily operations.

Application Service Providers (“ASPs”) should liaise with their respective backend Exchange Participants, Clearing Participants, Information Vendors and/or market data end-users, as applicable, to coordinate their participation in PRT . Exchange Participants and market data end-users relying on Information Vendors for market data used for trading purposes should also liaise with their respective Information Vendors to arrange the necessary market data support during PRT .

HKMC Annuity Limited (HKMCA), a wholly-owned subsidiary of The Hong Kong Mortgage Corporation Limited, announced today (17 November) the launch of the “Retire Well. Live Fully.” public education campaign. Dedicated to raising public awareness of the sustainable retirement lifestyle concept, the initiative features participation by pop trio “Grasshopper” (Calvin Choy, Remus Choy, and Edmond So).

To resonate with the public, the HKMCA has adapted “Grasshopper’s” classic hit “World Will Become Beautiful” (《世界會變得很美》) into a re-recorded version titled “Retire Well. Live Fully.” (《退休世界 變得很美》). Through the familiar melody and the trios’ personal reflections on entering a new stage of life, the HKMCA hopes to connect with the public’s aspirations for an ideal retirement and encourage people to build a sustainable retirement lifestyle that balances financial security, health, social well-being, and personal fulfillment.

Mr Daniel Leong, Executive Director and Chief Executive Officer of the HKMCA, said, “People in Hong Kong are living longer.

According to figures published by the Census and Statistics Department in 2026, a man aged 60 is expected to live to around 86 on average, and a woman of the same age to around 90.1 With retirement potentially spanning several decades, multi-dimensional planning for active ageing is essential to a ‘Sustainable Retirement’.

During production, the “Grasshopper” trio shared their thoughts on retirement.

items.source_excerpt:
To further strengthen the banking sector’s financing support for Northern Metropolis (NM) projects, the HKMA proposes to amend the Banking (Capital) Rules to designate government-related entities, including 11 post-secondary institutions and three park companies, as Domestic Public Sector Entities. This measure will help lower banks’ capital costs, assist these entities in obtaining bank financing, and thereby accelerate the implementation of NM projects. The HKMA intends to submit the amendments to the Legislative Council in the first quarter of 2027, with a view to their taking effect in the second quarter of the same year.

The Northern Metropolis Financial Advisory Taskforce (Taskforce), jointly established by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) and The Hong Kong Association of Banks (HKAB), convened its third meeting today (10 November). Meeting participants included representatives from the HKMA, HKAB, the Development Bureau, the Education Bureau (EDB), The Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau, the Innovation, Technology and Industry Bureau and 25 participating banks in the Taskforce (see Annex).

At the meeting, the EDB presented the latest development of the Northern Metropolis University Town (NMUT), including the positioning of the three university towns1, development of campus areas and related financial arrangements.

Background

10 November 2026

1 San Tin University Town, Hung Shui Kiu University Town and Ta Kwu Ling University Town.
